2. Brief facts as stated are that, appellant was plaintiff in O.S.no.493/1998 filed for specific performance of agreement of sale directing defendants to execute registered sale deed in respect of land bearing Sy.no.325, measuring 2 Acres 31 guntas, situated at Hinkal village ('suit property' for short).
3. In plaint, it was stated Muddamma, wife of late Rangappa of Kurubara Pete village, Kolar District was residing at Hinkal village in house of A. Papanna (plaintiff), since 1984.
It was stated suit property was ancestral property of defendants no.1 to 5, who intended to sell it.

On 29.08.1989 they executed agreement of sale in favour of Muddamma in respect of suit property agreeing to execute registered sale deed for total sale consideration of Rs.1,24,874/- by receiving Rs.5,000/- as advance sale consideration and agreeing to balance sale consideration at time of registration.

It was stated,
on 15.03.1990, they received further amount of Rs.15,000/- by NC: 2024:KHC:51282 endorsing same on agreement of sale and in view of provisions of Fragmentation Act, sought some more time to execute sale deed.
Thereafter on 12.05.1993, they received amount of Rs.75,000/- by executing shara.

It was stated defendant no.1 received Rs.29,875/- on behalf of other defendants and agreed to execute sale deed in favour of Muddamma within 4 years as suit property was notified for acquisition by MUDA.
4. It was further stated, in meanwhile Muddamma executed unregistered Will in favour of plaintiff on 10.10.1992 by transferring right, title and interest over suit property.
Thereafter, she went to Kolar and died on 26.08.1996.
After her death, plaintiff was given unregistered Will along with agreement of sale.

When, plaintiff approached defendants no.1 to 5 to execute registered sale deed,
they were postponing it.
On 19.08.1998, plaintiff got issued legal notice, but received untenable reply.
Hence, suit was filed.
5. On appearance, defendants no.1 to 5 filed common written statement denying plaint averments.
They stated Muddamma was total stranger to them and denied about her being tenant of plaintiff.
They admitted land bearing Sy.no.325 totally measuring 3 Acres 11 guntas was ancestral property of NC: 2024:KHC:51282 defendant no.1 and sub-divided into Sy.no.325/1.
They denied execution of Agreement of Sale and receipt of consideration.
It was stated, there was no privity of contract between defendants no.1 to 5 and Muddamma.
They specifically denied receipt of further sale consideration by executing shara.

They denied execution of Will by Muddamma in favour of plaintiff Sri. A Papanna vs Sri. Mayigowda on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76817470/
4 and alleged it was false and concocted, hence, plaintiff could not seek relief in absence of any agreement between defendants no.1 to 5 and Muddamma in respect of suit property.

6. It was stated Sy.no.325/1 of Hinkal village was absolute property of defendants no.1 to 5 and subject matter of acquisition by defendant no.7 (MUDA).
It was stated, defendants had challenged acquisition before this Court.
After acquisition, land was in possession of defendants no.8 and 9 - (KSRTC), which had built Bus Depot in it.
Hence, suit for specific performance was not maintainable and sought dismissal.
7. In its written statement - KSRTC, stated suit property was acquired by MUDA under Land Acquisition Act.
Since, plaintiff had not questioned acquisition.
In any case, NC: 2024:KHC:51282 challenge by owners was dismissed on 20.09.2012.
Thereafter, suit property was granted to KSRTC on lease for a period of 30 years by executing registered lease deed on 29.11.2012.
Possession certificate was issued on 22.12.2004/07.01.2013.
Thereafter, KSRTC had constructed Bus Depot at cost of 3 Crores.
Thus, suit property was already utilized for purposes for which it was acquired.

Hence, suit was not tenable.
8. Based on pleadings, trial Court framed following issues and addl. issues:
1) Whether the plaintiff proves that the defendants 1 to 3 have agreed to sell the suit schedule property to an extent of 2 acres 31 guntas under a agreement of sale dated 29.8.1989?
2) Whether the plaintiff further proves that the defendants have delivered the possession of suit schedule property to Muddamma?
3) Whether the plaintiff further proves that on 12.5.1993 the defendants have received a sum of Rs.75,000/- and executed a shara on the verse of agreement?
4) Whether the plaintiff further proves that Muddamma has executed a will in his favour on 10.10.1992 and by virtue of the same, he is entitled to get the relief of specific performance of contract?
5) Whether the plaintiff further proves that deceased Muddamma and he are ready and willing to perform their part of contract?
6) Whether the suit of the plaintiff is within time?

10. On consideration, trial Court answered issues no.1 to 5, 7, additional issues no.1 and 2 in negative and issue no.6 and additional issues no.3 and 4 in affirmative and issue no.8 by dismissing suit.
Aggrieved, plaintiff filed R.A.no.574/2014 on various grounds.

Based on same, first appellate Court framed following points:
1) Whether the lower Court was justified in holding that the execution of Will is not proved?
2) Whether lower Court was justified in holding that Ex.P.14 agreement of sale is not proved?
3) Whether the impugned judgment and decree calls for interference?
4) What order?
12. On consideration, it answered points no.1 and 2 in affirmative, point no.3 in negative and point no.4 by dismissing appeal.
Aggrieved, this appeal is filed.

13. Sri Anand K., learned counsel for plaintiff submitted, appeal was against concurrent findings in suit for specific performance of agreement of sale dated 29.08.1989 in respect of 2 Acres 31 guntas out of total extent of 3 Acres 11 guntas in Sy.no.325 of Hinkal village, executed by Muddamma and defendants no.1 to 5 which was subject matter of suit.
It was submitted in addition to advance sale Sri.

Sale - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:51282 deed could not be executed due to provisions of Fragmentation Act.
In meanwhile, Muddamma died executing Will bequeathing her rights under above agreement, to plaintiff.
It was submitted, though plaintiff was ready and willing to pay remaining sale consideration and called upon defendants to execute sale deed.
Defendants failed to come forward.
It was submitted, during pendency of suit, suit property was acquired by MUDA and handed over to KSRTC.
Nevertheless, plaintiff would be entitled for compensation, which was not appreciated by both Courts.

14. It was further submitted, since defendants no.1 to 5, themselves handed over Ex.P.1 - Will and Ex.P.14 - Agreement of Sale to plaintiff, there was no dispute about genuineness or execution of agreement of sale or Will.
It was submitted though Ex.D.11 would establish suit property was acquired, in cross-examination DW.1 admitted non-withdrawal of compensation.

Therefore, prayed for allowing appeal by relying on ratio in case of Sukhbir v. Ajit Singh, reported in (2021) 6 SCC 54.

It was submitted Will was not disputed.
Fact that no police complaint alleging forgery agreement of sale and Will.
Both Courts failed to appreciate admissions by PW.2 and DW.1 while considering validity of execution of agreement of sale - Ex.P.14.
Hence, following substantial questions of law would arise for consideration and sought for allowing appeal by answering same in favour of plaintiff.

"1. Whether both Courts erred in disbelieving Ex.P1 - Will on suspicious circumstance of disinheriting legal heirs, even when Will was not disputed by legal heirs even after compliance with Section 68 of Evidence Act and 63 of Succession Act?

2. Whether denial of relief of specific performance merely on ground that suit property was acquired, was contrary to ratio in Sukhbir's case (supra)?"
16.
Heard learned counsel and perused impugned judgment and decree.
17. This appeal is by plaintiff against concurrent findings dismissing suit for specific performance.
Admittedly, suit property belonged to defendants no.1 to 5.

In suit, plaintiff asserted that on 29.08.1989 defendants no.1 to 5 executed - 12 - Sri. A Papanna vs Sri. Mayigowda on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76817470/
7 NC: 2024:KHC:51282 Ex.P14 - agreement of sale in favour of Muddamma agreeing to sell suit property for Rs.1,24,874/-, by receiving Rs.5,000/- in advance and agreeing to execute registered sale deed by receiving balance sale consideration.

sentences.text: It was further stated, defendants no.1 to 5 received further sale consideration of Rs.15,000/- on 15.03.1990, by endorsing receipt on Ex.P14.

Likewise,
they received Rs.75,000/- on 12.05.1993 by executing shara.
Subsequently, defendant no.1 received Rs.29,875/- and agreed to execute sale deed within 4 years as suit property was pending acquisition by MUDA.
Plaintiff further stated, holder of agreement - Muddamma and her son - Venkatachala were tenants of plaintiff and well known and trusted by her.
On such consideration, she executed Ex.P1 - Will, bequeathing her right under Ex.P14 - agreement of sale to plaintiff, on 10.10.1992.
After her death on 20.08.1996, plaintiff as assignee demanded execution of sale deed by defendants no.1 to 5, as he was ready and willing to perform his part of it.
On denial, suit was filed.

18. Plaintiff examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Will dated 10.10.1992 as Ex.P1, death certificate of Muddamma as Ex.P2, legal notice with postal acknowledgments/receipts as - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:51282 Exs.P3 to P11, reply notice as Ex.P12, RPAD cover as Ex.P13, agreement of sale dated 29.08.1989 as Ex.P14, record of rights as Exs.P15 to P17 and application for de-notification as Ex.P18.
Attestor of Ex.P1 was examined as PW.2 to substantiate execution of Will and Venkatachala - son of Muddamma as PW.3 to establish valid assignment.

On other hand,
defendants no.1 to 5 comprehensively denied execution of agreement of sale, receipt of consideration as well as Will.
They contended suit was not tenable as suit property was acquired by MUDA.
19. Defendants no.8 and 9 - KSRTC contended suit property was acquired by MUDA granted to it on lease and it constructed Bus Depot.
To substantiate same, GPA holder of defendants no.1 to 5 deposed as DW.1, KSRTC official as DW.2 and SLAO of MUDA as DW.3.

They produced allotment letter as Ex.D3, receipt - Ex.D4, grant certificate - Ex.D5, possession certificate - Ex.D6, E.C - Ex.D7,
plan - Ex.D8, copy of lease- cum-sale deed as Ex.D9, final notification of acquisition as Ex.D11,
award and award notice as Exs.D12, 14 to D16, letter as Ex.D13, copy of payment register as Ex.D17.
20.

While passing judgment and decree, trial Court took up issues regarding execution of agreement of sale, delivery of - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:51282 possession, receipt of sale consideration, execution of Will, ready and willingness as well as entitlement for decree of specific performance, together.
It noted burden was on plaintiff.
Insofar as Ex.P1 - Will, it noted mere compliance with production of original obligation on Court examining validity of Will and examination of one attestor would not meet requirements of law.
Especially, when testator was stated to be a tenant of legatee and there was disinheritance of legal heirs of testator.
It observed obligation would be on legatee to explain suspicious circumstances.

It took note of admission by PW.1 that testator was not tenant, but, residing with her Sri. A Papanna vs Sri. Mayigowda on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76817470/
8 son, who was tenant of legatee.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: And further about testator having eight children.
It considered disinheritance as a grave suspicious circumstance.
Only explanation available was recital in Will about testator receiving financial and other help from legatee, but to prove which, PW.1 admitted there was no material.
It also referred to deposition of PW.3 about testator receiving pension and being financial independent to conclude failure on part of plaintiff to explain away suspicious circumstance.
Trial Court further observed correction of name of person to whom stamp papers on which Ex.P1 was drawn was without attestation.

It further noticed discrepancy in seal of - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC:51282 District Treasury and drew adverse inference for failure to examine stamp vendor to hold Ex.P1 as not proved.
21.
Even while examining Ex.P14 - agreement of sale, trial Court noted discrepancy about date of issuance of stamp paper by District Treasury.
It also observed, except recital in Ex.P14 there was no material to establish delivery of possession.
It also noted that there was no sufficient proof of Ex.P14 - agreement of sale, except PW.1.
It noted failure by plaintiff to elicit any admission from DW.1 about agreement.
Therefore, it concluded failure by plaintiff to establish agreement of sale or Will.
On said conclusion, it answered issues no.1 to 5 and 7 in negative.
It also held acquisition of suit property by MUDA and grant to KSRTC, would disentitle relief to plaintiff.
22. In appeal, first appellate Court on re-appreciation concurred with findings of trial Court.

Learned counsel for plaintiff sought to contend that dismissal of suit on ground of property being acquired would be unsustainable as held in Sukhbir's case (supra) that holder of agreement of sale would be entitled to receive compensation.
But, it is seen both Courts on detailed consideration held Will to be suffering from - 16 - NC: 2024:KHC:51282 suspicious circumstances and failure on part of plaintiff to explain them away.
Trial Court specifically observed failure by plaintiff to establish agreement of sale.

Admittedly,
PW.1 - plaintiff is not a party to Ex.P14, neither are PWs.2 and 3.

When defendants comprehensively denied execution of Ex.P14 and receipt of sale consideration as well as endorsement on it and burden cast under issues no.1 to 5 and 7 was on plaintiff, mere production of Ex.P14 - agreement of sale would not amount to proof.
Failure to prove agreement of sale would be fatal disentitling plaintiff even to relief for receiving compensation stated to be still in deposit.
Consequently, neither proposed substantial questions of law nor any other would arise for consideration.

Hence, following:
ORDER Appeal is dismissed without being admitted.
